meaning:
σπουδάζω
(σπουδή), [in LXX chiefly for בָּהַל ;]
to make haste; hence, to be zealous or eager, to give diligence: with inf. (see M, Pr., 205 f.), Gal.2:10, Eph.4:3, 1Th.2:17, 2Ti.2:15 4:9 4:21, Tit.3:12, Heb.4:11, 2Pe.1:10 3:14; with accusative and inf. (on this construction see Mayor in l; MM, xxiii), 2Pe.1:15 (for other constructions see LS, see word).†
(AS)

renderings.bsb: I will make every effort to ensure

elsewhere.note: They only asked us to remember the poor—which very thing I was also zealous to do.
being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
But we, brothers, being bereaved of you for a short season, in presence, not in heart, tried even harder to see your face with great desire,
Give diligence to present yourself approved by God, a workman who doesn’t need to be ashamed, properly handling the Word of Truth.
When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, be diligent to come to me to Nicopolis, for I have determined to winter there.
Let’s therefore give diligence to enter into that rest, lest anyone fall after the same example of disobedience.
Therefore, brothers, be more diligent to make your calling and election sure. For if you do these things, you will never stumble.
